A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HistoSelect and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material. Retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original HistoSelect benchmark results, a two-pathologist evaluation, qualitative examples, and component, token-budget, and loss-weight ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds macro-averaged metrics, sampling-distribution analysis, and training-strategy, Gemini, and ideal-group-selection experiments.

M1.justification: The CONCH tissue grouping, group sampler, patch selector, top-k selection, straight-through estimator, and implemented VQA plus two Bernoulli-KL losses remain unchanged. The hierarchical IB formulation revises the theoretical justification; the additional training and backbone experiments do not establish a replacement of the proposed method.

E1.justification: Section 4 revises SlideBench-VQA's reported coverage from 31 to 10 cancer types while retaining 4,560 WSIs, 176K question-answer pairs, and the official splits. All three datasets and their tasks remain; the PDFs do not establish that the underlying data changed. New analyses reuse existing coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds a Gemini 3 Flash comparison using random patches versus HistoSelect-selected patches in Table 12, plus an ideal-group-selection reference in Table 13. Comparator membership in the original benchmark and selection-mechanism comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: V3 adds macro-precision, macro-recall, and macro-F1 evaluation, extra-epoch sampler/selector training controls, and a frozen-Gemini experiment on 200 WSI-Bench cases with matched 100-patch inputs. It also introduces ideal-group controls and K-means/t-SNE analysis. These substantially extend evaluation design without replacing the original splits or preprocessing.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component, token-budget, and loss-weight ablations, v3 analyzes question-dependent sampling clusters, additional module-specific training, transfer to Gemini, and ideal group selection for single- versus multi-tissue questions. Sections 11.3–12 substantially expand mechanism and robustness investigations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The two-pathologist averaging procedure is retained; new macro metrics and cluster means do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive macro-metric results in Tables 7–8 and new findings in Tables 11–13, including Gemini accuracy of 59.5% with random patches versus 62.5% with selected patches under matched conditions. Sampling-cluster findings are also new. Table 1 revises SlideChat's morphology accuracy from 91.07 to 91.34; HistoSelect's original benchmark scores and retained ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 explicitly describes the two-level compression penalty as a heuristic decomposition. V3 introduces joint group/patch latent variables, a mutual-information chain-rule decomposition, conditional variational KL bounds, and a hierarchical objective, with a new derivation in supplementary Section 6, Equations 13–21.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: pathologist-inspired question-guided selection, interpretable evidence, approximately 70% fewer visual tokens, and superior performance across three datasets. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations connecting sampling clusters to four clinical question types, arguing for transfer across reasoning models, dedicated group-sampler optimization, and greater importance of group selection for multi-tissue reasoning. The existing limitations concerning dataset generalization and absent textual rationales are retained.

D1.justification: V3 adds a code-access link and documents stage-one projector/slide-encoder trainability, WSI-caption alignment data, a 1e-3 learning rate, three alignment epochs, and two second-stage epochs. Figure 7 discloses test-category counts. Previously stated batch size, second-stage learning rate, and warmup settings are relocated and retained; these disclosures do not establish changed original experiments.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces the efficiency-focused discussion of pruning, merging, FOCUS, PathVQ, and TCP-LLaVA with broader foundation-model and agent positioning, including PLIP, MUSK, Gecko, PathChat, PathFinder, WSI-Agents, and CpathAgent. It also adds hierarchical IB precedents. This substantially changes the comparison with prior research.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. V3 locally rewrites related work and the IB explanation, tightens several experimental paragraphs and the conclusion, relocates implementation details, expands the supplementary outline, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V3 adds five tables for macro metrics and new ablations, plus test-distribution, cluster-profile, and t-SNE figures. Existing qualitative figures and loss-weight tables are retained with renumbering and relocation. These additions substantially expand the visual presentation beyond minor caption and spacing edits.

improvement.justification: V3 improves empirical scrutiny through class-balanced metrics and targeted training, backbone, and group-selection checks, while additional training details and a code link improve reproducibility information. The gains are limited by absent uncertainty estimates and an underspecified ideal-group procedure. The new derivation leaves its connection to the implemented input-dependent similarity priors unclear, and the rewritten related work loses direct token-compression context.
